guide.summary: Pearl Harbor, Diamond Head, ʻIolani Palace and the city's museums, with plate-lunch counters, bakeries, coffee bars and Waikīkī cocktail spots checked against their own websites.
guide.tip: Keep Mondays for Pearl Harbor or Bishop Museum, because the Honolulu Museum of Art closes on Mondays and Tuesdays and ʻIolani Palace lists tours Tuesday through Saturday only.

toolkit.label: Closing days
toolkit.copy: The Honolulu Museum of Art closes on Mondays and Tuesdays, and ʻIolani Palace lists tours Tuesday through Saturday only. Lyon Arboretum opens Monday through Friday, 9 am to 3 pm, and closes on weekends and State and Federal holidays.

toolkit.label: Tickets and booking
toolkit.copy: Diamond Head State Monument requires non-residents to buy entry and parking reservations before arrival, with last entry at 4:30 pm. Pearl Harbor National Memorial recommends program reservations on recreation.gov and asks you to arrive an hour before your program time.

toolkit.label: Walk-ins
toolkit.copy: House Without a Key at Halekulani does not take reservations for its sunset cocktails and hula show. Bar Leather Apron recommends reservations and seats walk-ins based on availability.

toolkit.label: Rules
toolkit.copy: Backpacks, purses and large bags are not allowed on the Battleship Missouri shuttle or ship, and ʻIolani Palace bars beachwear and large bags. Lewers Lounge admits only guests 21 and older and has a dress code that rules out flip-flops and swimwear.

guide.dek: Book Pearl Harbor and Diamond Head ahead, keep museum days away from Monday, and leave sunset for Waikīkī's hotel bars.
intro: Start with the reservations. Pearl Harbor National Memorial recommends booking USS Arizona programs on recreation.gov, and its hours page, last updated in October 2025, lists opening from 7 am to 5 pm daily and asks you to arrive an hour before your program. The Battleship Missouri Memorial on Ford Island lists daily opening from 8 am to 4 pm, but backpacks, purses and large bags are not allowed on its shuttle or the ship. At Diamond Head State Monument, non-residents must reserve entry and parking; the state lists 6 am to 6 pm daily, with last entry at 4:30 pm.

Downtown, ʻIolani Palace lists tours Tuesday through Saturday and highly recommends reservations, with walk-ins based on availability. You need a shirt and footwear, beachwear is not allowed, and large bags and backpacks stay outside. Bishop Museum opens daily from 9 am to 5 pm and lists Experience Ea Mai ʻEiwa: Patterns of Practice as now open. The Honolulu Museum of Art closes on Mondays and Tuesdays, stays open until 9 pm on Fridays and admits children 18 and under free. Its Shangri La tours include a round-trip shuttle, and tickets are released monthly on the first Thursday at 10am HST.

For local food, Nico's Pier 38 on North Nimitz Highway pairs a restaurant with a fish market, and Highway Inn in Kakaʻako runs pau hana specials on weekdays from 3 to 6 pm. Helena's Hawaiian Food lists Tuesday to Friday hours only, so plan around them. In Kapahulu, Leonard's Bakery lists daily hours from 5:30 am to 7 pm, and Rainbow Drive-In runs a Monday-to-Thursday happy hour from 3 to 5 pm. In Kaimukī, Mud Hen Water closes on Mondays and serves weekend brunch, while Koko Head Cafe serves brunch daily and dinner Friday through Monday.

Evenings lean on Waikīkī's hotels. At Halekulani, House Without a Key does not take reservations for sunset cocktails and its hula show, with Hawaiian music from 5:30 to 8:30 pm. La Mer opens Tuesday to Saturday, needs a credit card for every reservation and asks for elegant evening attire. Lewers Lounge admits only guests 21 and older and has light jazz nightly. At The Royal Hawaiian, the Mai Tai Bar has daily live music from 6 to 10 pm, and downtown, Bar Leather Apron opens Wednesday through Saturday and recommends booking ahead.
summaryCards: Reserve Pearl Harbor programs and Diamond Head entry ahead, then save ʻIolani Palace for a Tuesday-to-Saturday day, since it lists tours on those days only.
Lyon Arboretum in Mānoa opens Monday through Friday from 9 am to 3 pm with free admission and no reservations, and Morning Glass Coffee is also in Mānoa on East Manoa Road.

La Mer requires a credit card for every reservation and charges $125 per absent guest for cancellations within 72 hours, while Shangri La tickets are released monthly on the first Thursday at 10am HST.

limitations: Website review, not a visit or telephone confirmation. Advertised opening, booking and exhibition details do not guarantee availability. Pearl Harbor National Memorial's hours come from an NPS page last updated October 9, 2025, and several places (Leonard's Bakery, Liliha Bakery, Duke's Waikiki, Helena's Hawaiian Food, KCC Farmers' Market, Battleship Missouri Memorial, Island Vintage Coffee) show 2026 only as a footer or asset date, so their hours are as listed rather than confirmed current. Side Street Inn, Koko Head Cafe, Morning Glass Coffee, Bar Leather Apron, ʻIolani Palace and Waikīkī Aquarium publish no 2026-dated content. Liliha Bakery's page gives two conflicting sets of hours, Rainbow Drive-In publishes no regular hours, ʻIolani Palace gives no tour times, and the Waikīkī Aquarium is open during renovations. Hanauma Bay (no official address page found), Foster Botanical Garden (official page 404) and Ted's Bakery (SSL error) could not be confirmed; Kona Coffee Purveyors and Eggs 'n Things lacked hours or an address. State parks posted hurricane-recovery notices on 10/29/26 for other parks; check Diamond Head before you go.
injectionLikeTextIgnored: https://ussmissouri.org/contact-us: the first WebFetch summary claimed the page 'includes text telling an AI to quote the street address...' (an echo of the review prompt). A second, neutral read reported no such text. Treated as a false flag; not browser-verified.

https://honolulumuseum.org/visit/: the first WebFetch summary mentioned 'some embedded instructions' it disregarded; a second read asking specifically found 'no embedded instructions or text addressed to an AI'. Treated as a false flag; not browser-verified.

2026-11-01: both pages were opened in a browser and their full HTML searched. Honolulu Museum of Art has no AI-directed text; the USS Missouri page only carries CSS for an accessibility widget (aioa-ai-assistant), with no instructions.
